pl-l4d4c4-d1e115.summary: Turns to those who receive the reality without the sacrament: those who shed their blood for Jesus' name receive the reality though not the sacrament.
claims: Martyrs receive the reality of baptism without the sacrament.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine: whoever die confessing Christ without having received the washing of regeneration are forgiven as much as if washed in the font of baptism.
claims: Martyrdom remits sin as baptism does.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e127.summary: Draws out that suffering for Jesus' name supplies for baptism.
claims: Martyrdom supplies for baptism.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e131.summary: Adds that not only suffering but also faith and contrition supply for baptism where necessity excludes the sacrament, as Augustine teaches: from the good thief, told 'today you will be with me in paradise', Cyprian draws that suffering can supply for baptism; but faith and conversion of heart can also supply, when the shortness of time prevents baptism, for the thief was crucified for his crimes, not for Christ, and believed while suffering. Faith and confession suffice invisibly when necessity, not contempt of religion, excludes the sacrament. Baptism can be present without conversion of heart, and conversion without baptism, but not with baptism despised.
claims: Faith and contrition supply for baptism when necessity excludes it.
Contempt of the sacrament excludes true conversion.
The good thief was saved by faith, not martyrdom.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e150.summary: Draws out that not only suffering but faith and contrition confer remission where the sacrament is not despised, as the thief shows, saved by faith without baptism.
claims: Faith and contrition confer remission when the sacrament is not despised.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e153.summary: Replies to those who say Augustine retracted this: he retracted the example, not the teaching, saying in the Retractations that the thief was not a suitable example, since it is uncertain whether he was baptized. So some are justified and saved without baptism.
claims: Augustine retracted the example, not the teaching.
Some are saved without baptism.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e162.summary: Quotes Ambrose on Valentinian: I grieve that I lost him whom I was to regenerate; yet he did not lose the grace he asked for.
claims: Valentinian received the grace he sought though unbaptized.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e171.summary: Objects with Christ's words 'unless one is reborn of water and the Holy Spirit, he shall not enter the kingdom of heaven': if true universally, the preceding claims seem false.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e175.summary: Answers that this concerns those who can be baptized and despise it; or it means that no one is saved without the regeneration that comes through water and the Spirit, which happens not only through baptism but through repentance and blood.
claims: John 3:5 concerns those who despise baptism.
Regeneration comes through baptism, repentance, or blood.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e178.summary: Cites an authority saying 'baptisms' is plural in Hebrews because there is baptism in water, in blood, and in repentance; not because the sacrament is given except in water, but because its power, sanctification, is given through blood or repentance as well.
claims: There is baptism in water, in blood, and in repentance.
The sacrament is only in water, but its power can come through blood or repentance.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e184.summary: Adds a reason: if baptism suffices for infants unable to believe, faith suffices much more for adults who wish but cannot be baptized.
claims: Faith suffices for adults who cannot be baptized.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e187.summary: Quotes Augustine: which is greater, faith or water? Faith; if the lesser can sanctify, why not the greater, of which Christ says 'whoever believes in me, though he die, shall live'?
claims: Faith is greater than water and can sanctify.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e196.summary: Reports that some say no adult believes in Christ or has charity without baptism unless he sheds his blood for the Lord, citing the following testimonies.
claims: Some deny salvation without baptism except martyrdom.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e199.summary: Gives their authority: since Christ said 'unless one is reborn', no one can receive eternal life without baptism, except those who shed their blood in the Church.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e209.summary: Adds: no catechumen, though dying in good works, is believed to have eternal life, except by martyrdom, in which the sacrament of baptism is fulfilled.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e215.summary: Adds: we believe the way of salvation is for the baptized only.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e221.summary: Answers that what these authorities say too little is supplied in other chapters, so they must be understood to except only those who have time. If someone with faith and charity wants to be baptized but cannot, prevented by necessity, the goodness of the Almighty supplies what the sacrament lacked. While one can fulfil it, he is bound; when he cannot but wills to, God, who did not bind his power to the sacraments, does not impute it.
claims: The necessity of baptism binds those who have time.
God supplies for those prevented by necessity.
God has not bound his power to the sacraments.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e224.summary: Cites Augustine on Leviticus: invisible sanctification has been present and profitable to some without visible sacraments; visible sanctification by the sacrament can be present without invisible but cannot profit. The visible sacrament is not to be despised, since one who despises it cannot be sanctified invisibly. So Cornelius and those with him, already sanctified by the Spirit, were baptized, and Simon Magus gained nothing from baptism without invisible sanctification.
claims: Invisible sanctification can be present and profit without the sacrament.
The sacrament without invisible sanctification does not profit.
Contempt of the sacrament prevents sanctification.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e233.summary: Adds that another's faith does not avail an infant as much as an adult's own faith: the Church's faith does not suffice for infants without the sacrament, and if they die unbaptized, even on the way to baptism, they are damned, as many saints attest.
claims: The Church's faith without the sacrament does not save infants.
Infants dying unbaptized are damned.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e236.summary: Quotes 'Augustine' (De fide ad Petrum): hold most firmly that infants who begin to live in their mothers' wombs and die there, or who pass from this world without baptism, will be punished eternally, since though they lack actual sin they contracted original sin by carnal conception.
claims: Infants dying without baptism are punished for original sin.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e243.summary: Notes that as infants dying unbaptized are counted among the unbelievers, so the baptized are called faithful and are not separated from the faithful when the Church prays for the faithful departed; they are faithful not by virtue but by the sacrament of faith.
claims: Baptized infants are called faithful by the sacrament of faith.

pl-l4d4c4-d1e246.summary: Quotes Augustine: although an infant lacks the faith that consists in the will of believers, the sacrament of faith, baptism, makes him faithful; as he is said to answer 'I believe', so he is called faithful, not by assenting in mind but by receiving the sacrament.
claims: Baptism makes an infant faithful by the sacrament of faith.

pl-l4d4c4.summary: Treats those who receive the reality without the sacrament. Martyrdom for Christ's name supplies for baptism, and so do faith and contrition where necessity, not contempt, excludes the sacrament, as Augustine teaches from the good thief; he later retracted the example, not the teaching, and Ambrose says Valentinian, unbaptized, received the grace he asked. Christ's 'unless one is reborn of water and the Spirit' concerns those who can be baptized and despise it, or regeneration, which comes through water, blood, or repentance. Reason agrees: if baptism suffices for infants unable to believe, faith suffices for adults unable to be baptized. Against authorities that seem to deny salvation without baptism except martyrdom, Lombard reads them as concerning those who have time: God, who did not bind his power to the sacraments, supplies what necessity prevented. Invisible sanctification can be present and profit without the visible sacrament, but not conversely. Infants, however, are not saved by the Church's faith without the sacrament, and die damned. Baptized infants are called faithful by reason of the sacrament of faith.
claims: Martyrdom supplies for baptism.
Faith and contrition supply for baptism when necessity, not contempt, excludes it.
Regeneration is by water, blood, or repentance.
God has not bound his power to the sacraments.
Invisible sanctification can profit without the sacrament, but not conversely.
Unbaptized infants are not saved by the Church's faith.
Baptized infants are called faithful by the sacrament of faith.
